name: Rufina Sedillo
equipment: Buckskin coat that was her husband's, cut down, over a black dress and a man's leather leggings
Repeating rifle (Winchester 1873, .44), which she bought with the wool money in 1880 after the wolves took forty ewes
Bowie knife in her belt, which she uses for everything from shearing to supper
Mule: Pancha, grey, sure-footed and old, who knows every arroyo on the commons better than Rufina does
A shepherd's staff, a sling she can kill a coyote with at forty paces, and a canteen
Three herders and four dogs, who are not equipment and would be offended
Her husband's water-right paper on the acequia madre, and a list in her own hand of every spring on the commons and who waters there
A rosary, a packet of piñon nuts and a twist of chile in her pocket
features: Hard Country (Frontier-Born origin: advantage on saving throws against exhaustion from heat, cold, thirst and hard travel; needs half the usual water one day in three; once per long rest shrugs off a level of trail exhaustion; her rations last half again as long)

Trailcraft (Scout: never lost on the commons or any terrain she has crossed, by day or night; finds water for herself, her companions and her animals each day without a check; follows a trail at a normal pace, learning how many, how long ago, and whether shod, loaded or lame; her party can't become lost while she guides it)
Long Shot (Scout: no disadvantage at long range with a Longarm if she Aimed first this turn; proficiency doubled for Perception checks to spot something more than 300 ft away)

Ghost on the Range (Scout, 2nd level: in natural terrain she can Hide as a bonus action, and hide when only lightly obscured; no Stealth disadvantage at a normal travel pace; leaves no trail anyone without Trailcraft can follow unless she chooses)
Path: Guide (Scout, 3rd level: her party travels at a hard pace without exhaustion, finds forage and grass for its animals on any terrain that has any, and has advantage on saves against weather)
Ability Score Improvement (Scout, 4th level: +1 Dexterity, +1 Wisdom)

Proving Up (Homesteader background: farm, ranch and sheep-camp families anywhere give her a meal and a place by the fire and tell her who has been threatening whom; she knows the acequia's rules, the commons' rules and water rights better than most lawyers, and what it means when a company fences a spring)

personality.traits: I say what I think, once, and then I expect it to be done. I trust animals sooner than men and weather sooner than either. I do not smile at strangers and I feed everyone.
personality.ideals: The springs and the pastures are in common, for all. My husband's grandfather's grandfather was given them that way, and I will hand them on that way or die on the commons.
personality.bonds: My two thousand sheep and the three families who herd them. The boy Tiburcio, whom I have hidden in my loft. My Ramón, who has been dead four years and still tells me what to do.
personality.flaws: I have kept a secret for two years that could save the grant, because it would shame my husband's memory and the Lucero name both. I am too proud to be told I am wrong, and too angry to listen when I am right.

appearance: A tall, rawboned woman of thirty-eight with a weathered brown face, grey streaks in a heavy black braid, a strong nose and very steady black eyes. A cut-down buckskin coat over black, a man's flat hat tied under her chin with a black ribbon, and a rifle she carries as if it were a broom.
backstory: Rufina Sedillo was born Rufina Abeyta in 1843 at Los Ranchitos, three miles up the river from the plaza, and at nineteen she married Ramón Sedillo, whose family had grazed sheep on the commons of the Merced de Santa Teresita since the beginning. Ramón served on the grant's comisión, and when he died of pneumonia in the winter of 1877 Rufina refused every offer for his sheep and his water right, including Don Fermín Lucero's, and ran them herself with three families of herders who had worked for Ramón. She is the only woman who owns a herd on the commons, and the herders call her la patrona, which she pretends to dislike. She knows every arroyo, spring and sheep trail from the Cerro Colorado to the Sierra Prieta. In 1879, when Don Fermín asked the comisión to lend the grant's papers to his lawyer, Ramón's old friend Don Policarpio gave them up, and Rufina did not tell him that the most important of them, the act of possession, was not among them, because Ramón had taken it out years before and walled it up beside her fireplace. On the night of 30 June Tiburcio Archibeque rode into her camp half dead with fear, and she has hidden him since and told the herders she will skin anyone who talks. (Companion. Hooks: Tiburcio; the fence at the Ojo del Gato; the paper in her wall.)

dmNotes.roleplaying: Rufina is the commons made into a person: hard, generous, practical and furious. Use her to show the party what the grant is for. She knows where every spring is, who waters there and what a fence on the Ojo del Gato would do to forty families. She is the party's guide on the commons and their best tracker (Trailcraft, Guide), and the person most likely to lead the vaqueros to cut the fence, so a party that wants to stop that has to convince her. She does not trust the patrón, the Company, the Americans or the party, in that order, until they earn it.
dmNotes.voice: Low, flat and decided, in Spanish, with very little English and no patience for it. Short sentences. Calls the sheep by name, the dogs by name, and men by their surnames. When she approves of something she says "Bueno," once, and that is high praise.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: keep the springs open and the commons in common. Secondary: keep Tiburcio alive. Tertiary: honour Ramón, which she has come to understand might mean giving up his secret.
dmNotes.secrets: The act of possession of 1768 is walled up in the niche beside her fireplace, in a tin box (CLUE E5, st-scenario-002). She gives it up only to people who have earned her trust with the boy, at the junta, or by treating her as the person in charge. Second secret: in 1878 Ramón signed a letter at Don Fermín's request calling him "principal heir of the founder", and the Company has it. She is afraid it will lose the grant. It will not, because a courtesy to a patrón is not a deed, and Licenciado Montaño can tell her so. Third: she has been sending a herder's boy to watch the Company's fence crew since the morning they arrived, and she knows exactly how many guards there are and when they change.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: suspicious, then fiercely loyal. Toward Tiburcio: a hard aunt who would kill for him. Toward Nicanor, if played: fond, and exasperated by his stake-pulling. Toward Don Fermín: cold, for reasons she will not give, until he breaks with the Company, and then she gives him the paper herself. Toward Victoriano Romero: an old acquaintance; her sheep and Laguna's have shared a boundary pasture all her life, and they argue about it every spring with great mutual respect. Toward the Company: hatred.
